correctness.rationale: For all integers m,n>=2, the intact biclique cut kernel is delta_{i,k}/n+delta_{j,l}/m-1/(mn). The added edge lies in a Laplacian eigenmode of eigenvalue n; Sherman–Morrison on zero-sum vertices gives the exact rank-one pseudoinverse update. Three complete edge orbits determine all cut/cycle absolute column sums. A direct algebraic comparison identifies both unrestricted orbit maxima and the five-zone integer thresholds for n>=5. Diagonal cut entries are in (0,1) for the complement calculation. The standalone exact-Fraction program reconstructs grounded Laplacians for 58 parameter pairs and checks 1858 columns, with terminal output GRAPH_PROJECTION_CERTIFICATE_OK. Finite enumeration is corroborative, not a proof of all n,m.

value.rationale: The norm sensitivity of canonical graph cut/cycle projections is a natural operator invariant of transportation-cost/Lipschitz-free graph structures. A single intrapart addition yields five sharply separated regimes for every fixed n>=5, including the exceptional decrease of a cut-projection norm, a wide double plateau, a cycle-only growth interval, and joint growth with an exact three-step onset difference. These are complete infinite-family structural thresholds, not a one-instance numerical recomputation or a relabeling of the known biclique formulas; potential use is in studying stability of graph transport-space projections under sparse perturbations.
